transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-06-11
Start: 15:00 PDT
Duration: 52 minutes
Attendees: Maya Singh (Redwood AE), Ethan Cole (Redwood SE), Lena Cho (Opal - Head of ML), Marco Ruiz (Opal - CTO), Sarah Patel (Opal - PM)

Automated Summary (auto-generated, may be rough):
Redwood and Opal scoping POC. Agreed on 4-week POC with kickoff, access setup, baseline benchmarks, mid-point review and executive readout. Success criteria: p95 latency < 150ms for 512 tokens on hosted or dedicated equivalent, throughput 50 req/s sustained with batching, model quality F1 > 0.82 on labeled eval set, and cost target < $X per 100k tokens. Security: SOC2, SSO, KMS requirements noted. Next: SOW, kickoff, access checklist, sample dataset.

Topics: POC timeline & milestones, success criteria, workload sizing, benchmark plan, security/access, decision gates

Action items (captured separately): see metadata section

Transcript:
[00:00] Maya (Redwood): Hey everyone, thanks for joining, we're excited to scope the POC with Opal, the plan today is to line up success criteria, sizing, and a timeline with milestones.
[00:15] Lena (Opal): Thanks Maya, yup, we're looking to evaluate Redwood for our customer support summarization pipeline — throughput and cost are the big blockers right now.
[00:28] Ethan (Redwood SE): Cool, can you give a quick sense of current stack and volume?
[00:33] Marco (Opal): Sure, right now we have a mix of on-prem GPUs and cloud infra. We ingest ~120k customer messages a day, peak single-tenant concurrency around 60 rps, average request size is 150 tokens, tails up to 800 tokens for long threads.
[00:49] Sarah (Opal): The key metric for product is latency under 200ms p95 for short flows, but ML team wants to aim lower if possible — they mentioned 150ms p95 as ideal.
[01:05] Ethan: ok, that helps. For POC we'll size workloads for both short (<=256 tokens) and long (512-800) sequences. Our suggested test matrix: 1) baseline hosted low-latency run, 2) dedicated GPU run with batching + KV cache, 3) quantized variant for cost test.
[01:25] Speaker 1: Mm-hmm, and — and what about security?
[01:29] Maya: Good point, Opal's asked about SOC2 and KMS. We can provide SOC2 report and we support customer-managed KMS for Private. For Hosted flows we offer encryption at rest and in transit; for Dedicated/Private we can do VPC peering and customer-managed keys.
[01:46] Lena: We will need audit logs and SSO integration — SAML. Also data residency for EU customers, but initial POC can be us-east.
[01:58] Ethan: Noted. For the POC success criteria, can we confirm the list so we're aligned?
[02:03] Marco: Yeah, main ones — 1) model output quality not regress > 5% vs current baseline on our labeled set, 2) latency p95 < 150ms for 256 tokens on target infra OR equivalent throughput on Dedicated, 3) cost within target (we'll define with your pricing), and 4) integration readiness (simple API and rollout plan).
[02:22] Maya: That sounds good. I'll capture those as the official scoping success criteria.
[02:27] Lena: Also want to verify fallback behavior — if Dedicated is constrained, auto-fallback to hosted with graceful degradation?
[02:34] Ethan: Yes we can demo routing policies and automatic fallback to a compatible variant. There may be a slight change in latency when falling back, we'll quantify during the benchmark.

[05:10] Ethan: Proposed POC timeline (4 weeks):
- Week 0 (Kickoff): 2026-06-23 (kickoff meeting + access setup)
- Week 1 (Access + Baseline): 2026-06-24 to 2026-06-30 (access setup, run baseline hosted tests)
- Week 2 (Perf & Scale): 2026-07-01 to 2026-07-07 (dedicated runs, batching, quantization tests)
- Week 3 (Mid-point review): 2026-07-08 (midpoint demo + adjustments)
- Week 4 (Wrap & Exec Readout): 2026-07-15 to 2026-07-21 (final results + exec readout 2026-07-21)

[05:50] Sarah: That's tight but doable. We need the sample dataset and infra contacts for VPC.
[05:55] Marco: We'll share dataset and security contact this week.
[06:02] Maya: Great, for access options we need to confirm which path — Hosted API with sample topline, Dedicated (reserved) capacity, or Private VPC. For the POC we recommend Hosted + Dedicated comparison unless you require on-prem.
[06:18] Lena: Probably Hosted + Dedicated is fine. We want to understand the cost delta.

[09:30] Ethan: Benchmark specifics we'll run: latency distributions (p50/p95/p99), throughput sustained over 10-minute windows, cold start metrics, token-level cost estimates, and output quality metrics (exact match, F1, human eval spot checks). We'll also include KV cache warm/cold runs to show improvements on chat-like flows.
[09:56] Speaker 2: How many samples — like number of requests?
[10:00] Ethan: We're thinking about 10k sample requests for baseline, with stratified sizes: 70% short (<256), 20% mid (256-512), 10% long (>512). If you can provide labeled eval (~2k labeled examples) we can compute change in F1.

[12:10] Lena: For cost analysis, give us both per-token and per-100k token estimates. Also show how batching and quantization affect both latency and cost.
[12:22] Maya: We'll include cost sensitivity charts in the final readout.

[15:00] Marco: On network side, we'll need a firewall rule and a contact for the infra team; can you share the IP ranges and peering steps?
[15:10] Maya: Yes, we'll send the secure access checklist and firewall/IP ranges. For VPC peering we typically need a small window to validate routes — recommend scheduling with your infra team during Week 0.

[18:45] Ethan: Decision gates at midpoint: if the ded-provisioned throughput isn't within 20% of target we'll iterate model configs or increase dedicated capacity. Exec readout will include final recommendation: go-live, further tuning, or pilot extension.

[21:30] Sarah: Who should attend the mid-point review? Product, ML lead, and infra?
[21:35] Maya: Yes, recommend ML lead (Lena), CTO (Marco) for exec readout, and product (Sarah) for mid-point. We'll send calendar invites.

[30:00] Maya: Quick note on metrics thresholds we propose to lock in: p95 latency <= 150ms for 256-token flows on Dedicated (or <200ms on Hosted), throughput >= 50 req/s sustained with batching, quality delta <= 5% F1 drop versus baseline. Cost target: TBD, we'll propose scenarios in SOW.

[36:12] Marco: If we see model quality regressions we'll need to know rollback procedures and version pinning.
[36:20] Ethan: Absolutely — rollout policies, model pinning and canary are in the console. We'll demo automatic fallback and rollback in the mid-point session.

[42:00] Lena: Any blockers for data privacy? We need to confirm retention and deletion policies for the POC.
[42:08] Maya: We can ensure logs are retained per agreement, and for PII we can scrub or use customer-provided KMS. We'll include data retention terms in SOW.

[47:55] Sarah: Next steps recap?
[48:00] Maya: Recap: 1) I'll send SOW + pricing by 6/14, 2) send secure access checklist by 6/13, 3) Ethan will share benchmark plan and test harness by 6/18, 4) Opal to provide sample dataset and infra contacts by 6/15, 5) schedule kickoff 6/23.
[48:22] Marco: Sounds good.
[48:25] Lena: Thanks everyone, looking forward.
[48:30] Maya: Thanks all, we'll follow up in email and slack. Bye.

End of transcript.

Success criteria (captured):

- Latency: p95 <= 150ms for 256-token flows on Dedicated (<=200ms on Hosted)
- Throughput: sustained >= 50 req/s with batching
- Cost: within target range to be defined in SOW (show scenarios)
- Operational: API + SSO + audit logs in place for rollout
